newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: S&P arm lifts Australian dollar risk factors-paper.
newsitem.headline: S&P arm lifts Australian dollar risk factors-paper.

text.p: The research group of Standard and Poor's ratings agency, DRI/McGraw Hill, has increased the risks that the Australian dollar could experience a significant depreciation against the U.S. dollar, the Australian Financial Review newspaper said in a report from London on Wednesday.

The paper said that DRI's latest global currency risk research had assigned a 15 percent risk probability that the Australian dollar will depreciate by 25 percent against the U.S. dollar over the next year, and a 45 percent risk factor over the next five years.
Those risk factors are higher than the previous factors of 10 and 43 percent respectively.
DRI rated Australia's current account/external debt and export growth as high risk, and said that "Australia was in the process of losing its status as a 'high yielding' currency".

"On a five-year horizon, the chronic external deficit and dependence on volatile commodity export dollars leaves the currency at a moderate risk of depreciation, despite the Reserve Bank's stabilising efforts," the paper quoted the report as saying.
An S&P spokeswoman in the Melbourne regional office said she could not immediately verify the report and would contact the New York head office for further comment.
